title: Ops Orchestra: Company-wide Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, and Travel Procedures
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document (Ops Orchestra) defines the canonical, company-wide procedures for access and permissions, change management, data classification & handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding & management, travel policy, and a small library of standard templates. It is intended for managers, approvers, and people-ops/finance partners who execute or govern cross-functional operational processes.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors that require platform, finance, or HR-related access or services. Exceptions must be approved by the relevant owner_team and logged in the change registry.

Owners and SLAs
- Document owner: finance-legal
- Primary operational leads: Security (access changes), Eng-SRE (infrastructure change runs), Finance (procurement/expenses), People-Ops (travel & benefits)
- Target SLA for routine approvals: 72 business hours
- Emergency/expedited approvals: same-day (see Emergency change section)

1) Access & Permissions
1.1. Access model
- Roles: Employee, Contractor, Service (machine identity), Admin
- Principle of least privilege (PoLP) is required for all roles. Role permissions must be justified in the access request ticket.
- Temporary access: granted using time-bound roles (max 14 days for privileged work).

1.2. Request and approval flow
1. Submit access request via internal access-portal (link: /internal/tools/access-portal). Include: owner, justification, resources, duration, and approver group.
2. Security review: Security reviews high-scope requests (production, key stores, billing).
3. Grant: System auto-provisions where templates exist; otherwise manual provisioning by Cloud Ops within SLA.
4. Verification: Requester confirms access; owner_team marks request closed.

1.3. Access matrix (example)
| Resource class | Typical roles allowed | Approval required | Max duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Production inference cluster | Platform-engineer, Release-engineer | Security + Team Lead | 7 days (expirable) |
| Billing and invoices | Finance, Accounting | Finance Manager | 30 days |
| Audit logs / SIEM | Security | Security Lead | 14 days |
| Private console (VPC) | Customer Success (with customer consent) | Security + Customer Success Director | 14 days |

1.4. Periodic review
- Quarterly entitlement review for Admin and privileged roles. Teams must certify access within 10 business days of quarterly notification.

2) Change Management
2.1. Classification
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-approved templates, no downtime (automated).
- Normal change: scheduled, requires change ticket and 72-hour review window.
- Emergency change: unplanned, immediate action required to restore availability or reduce security risk. Must be retrospectively reviewed by CAB.

2.2. Change Advisory Board (CAB)
- Membership: Eng-SRE, Platform, Security, Product, and one Finance/Legal representative.
- Weekly meeting cadence for normal changes; emergency convened ad-hoc.
- Approval criteria: risk, roll-back plan, test plan, owner, monitoring & alerting updates.

2.3. Change request template (required fields)
- Title
- Owner & approvers
- Type (standard/normal/emergency)
- Rollout window & maintenance window
- Backout/rollback plan
- Canary/verification steps and SLOs to observe
- Impacted services and customers

2.4. Deployment checklist (example)
1. Create change ticket in change-registry (link: /internal/tools/change-registry).
2. Attach runbook and rollback commands.
3. Confirm tests in staging and smoke tests.
4. Schedule and notify stakeholders 48 hours before the window.
5. Execute canary rollout; monitor latency/error metrics for 30 minutes.
6. Proceed to full rollout if health criteria met, otherwise initiate rollback.

3) Data Classification & Management
3.1. Classification levels
- Public: Safe for external publication.
- Internal: Company-internal operational data; limited sharing outside Redwood prohibited.
- Confidential: Business-sensitive data (contracts, pricing, non-public benchmarks).
- Restricted: Regulated or customer-sensitive data (PII, PHI, encrypted customer payloads).

3.2. Handling rules by class
- Storage: Restricted must be stored in customer-dedicated or encrypted buckets with KMS key rotation; Confidential must use company-managed encryption.
- Access: Restricted requires two-factor and documented business justification.
- Transit: TLS 1.2+; internal tunnels must be encrypted and use mutual authentication where possible.
- Retention: See table below.

3.3. Retention & Disposal (summary)
| Data class | Default retention | Disposal action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public | N/A | No action required |
| Internal | 3 years | Archive to long-term internal store, remove direct access |
| Confidential | 7 years | Secure delete and log shred event |
| Restricted | Customer-specific / regulatory | Follow customer or legal retention schedule; certify deletion with KMS key rotation |

3.4. Data breach playbook (high level)
1. Contain: Isolate affected resources.
2. Notify: Security incident channel and CISO.
3. Assess: Determine scope and classification of exposed data.
4. Remediation: Revoke credentials, rotate keys, patch vulnerability.
5. Notification: Legal decides customer/regulator notifications.
6. Post-incident: Postmortem and remediation tracking.

4) Procurement & Expenses
4.1. Procurement thresholds & approval matrix
- Purchase Request (PR) < $5,000: Manager approval (auto in procurement system).
- $5,000 – $50,000: Finance Manager + Procurement review.
- $50,000 – $250,000: Procurement Director + Legal review.
- > $250,000: VP-level approval and board notification for multiyear commitments.

4.2. Preferred vendors and vendor rationalization
- Teams should use preferred vendors list in procurement portal. If a new vendor is required, request a Vendor Exception with justification and complete the risk questionnaire.
- Vendor Exception approvals target SLA: 5 business days.

4.3. Expense policy highlights
- Travel expenses must include original receipts for amounts > $75.
- Per diem and caps: domestic $80/day, international $120/day unless pre-approved.
- Pre-approval: Any trip with total estimated cost > $2,000 requires manager + Finance pre-approval.

4.4. Purchase order & invoice flow (example)
1. Create PR in procurement system with line items and cost center.
2. Procurement reviews contracts, confirms compliance and insurance.
3. Contract owner (Legal) signs if required.
4. PO issued to vendor; invoice matched in AP and paid per vendor terms.

4.5. Template: minimal Purchase Request JSON (for internal procurement portal)
{
  "title": "[short description]",
  "requested_by": "user@example.com",
  "cost_center": "ENG-PLATFORM",
  "amount": "$[amount]",
  "vendor": "VendorName",
  "justification": "[business reason]"
}

5) Vendor Onboarding & Management
5.1. Onboarding checklist (must-complete before PO issuance)
- Vendor risk questionnaire completed and scored.
- Security controls validated: SOC2 or equivalent, encryption-at-rest, vulnerability disclosure policy.
- Contractual terms (SLA, liability caps, data residency) negotiated.
- Approved insurance certificates on file.
- Finance payment terms and tax forms collected.

5.2. Ongoing vendor review
- Quarterly business reviews for strategic vendors.
- Annual security re-attestation for vendors holding Confidential or Restricted data.
- Termination checklist: data return/secure deletion, credential revocation, final invoice reconciliation.

6) Travel & Meetings Policy
6.1. Booking and approvals
- All business travel should be booked via the company travel portal (link: /internal/tools/travel).
- Manager approval required for all travel. International travel requires People-Ops pre-check for visa and safety guidance.

6.2. Health, safety, and insurance
- Company travel insurance covers itinerary-based medical and evacuation for approved trips. Register your travel itinerary in travel-portal to enable support.

6.3. Sustainable travel guidance
- When feasible, prefer direct flights with lower emissions (use carbon-light options in travel portal). Combine trips for adjacent meetings rather than separate travel instances.

7) Templates & Forms (library)
- Access request template: /templates/access-request.md (example fields: resource, justification, approvers, duration)
- Change request template: /templates/change-request.md
- Purchase Request JSON template: (see section 4.5)
- Vendor risk questionnaire: /templates/vendor-questionnaire.pdf

8) Exceptions, Escalations, and Audit
- Exceptions: Submit policy exceptions to finance-legal with documented business justification and compensating controls. Exceptions have a 6-month default expiry unless renewed.
- Escalations: Use the incident/escalation matrix for operational disputes; unresolved cases route to Director-level owners.
- Audit: Teams must retain change and procurement records for at least 3 years and be able to produce them for internal or external audit.

9) Frequently asked operational scenarios (quick answers)
- Need temporary production access for a P0 fix? Open an Emergency change and tag Security + Eng-SRE, provide rollback and verification steps.
- New contractor requiring billing console access? Use contractor role template and limit to 14 days; require Finance sponsor and sign-off.
- Vendor wants to store customer payloads? Require Restricted data handling controls and a customer-approved data processing addendum (DPA).

10) Change log & related artifacts
- Major revisions: 2026-09-12: Added vendor re-attestation cadence and procurement thresholds update.
- Artifact links: change-registry, procurement-portal, access-portal, vendor-portal (internal links in system).

Appendix A: Contacts and escalation list
- Security (access changes, incidents): security-oncall@redwood.ai
- Procurement & Vendor ops: procurement@redwood.ai
- Finance (expenses): expenses@redwood.ai
- People-Ops (travel & visas): people-ops@redwood.ai
- CAB coordinator: cab@redwood.ai

Appendix B: Short CLI snippets
- Revoke an API key (example):
  curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"key_id":"abcd-1234"}'

- Query change registry for open emergency changes:
  curl -sS https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/changes?status=emergency | jq '.'

Appendix C: Quick checklist PDF export (one-pager summary)
- Use the export template in /templates/ops-onepager.docx to produce a manager-facing checklist for onboarding new hires, vendors, or services.

End of document.
